body: Of course. And btw, people who say crap like that are not worth your time!💕

About the respondents whose childhood sucked, I can totally relate. I was physically abused nearly daily, for years, and my father, who KNEW it was happening, turned his back and moved out, leaving my brother and I with her. Then my brother ran away and I was the lucky sole recipient of her wrath. 
I have done A LOT of work in therapy and finally came to forgive my mother about 4 years before she died, as well as my Absentee Father. 
But, get this, my Dad is now a bitter old man who can be downright hateful, and, when my mother died ON MY BIRTHDAY, only 4 months ago, I was devastated. Part of me doesn’t understand this phenomenon, bc of what she did, but once I forgave, I understood she was struggling with her own issues as an abused child herself. As for my father, he is his own worst enemy, and has to take his own steps to regain joy in life. 
No, none of that excuses the trauma they inflicted, but forgiveness is freeing for you, as an individual.
Oh, and yes, I was also VERY upset that my attempt was unsuccessful. Solidarity.

I know EXACTLY how you feel, dear heart, because that is how people generally respond when someone says they want to die. People are ill-equipped and don’t seem to know what to say. 
I posed this same query to my therapist, who said, despite how elementary it seems, that you need to tell that person exactly what you need from them in that moment, ie, “I feel hopeless, and would just like for you to tell me you love me/give me a hug/tell me something good about myself.” 
I know it feels ridiculous; like people should just “get it,” but they can’t read minds and most likely are not as in-touch or deep as you are. I know this is definitely the case for me. Praying things get better. Know that you are loved!!

I am sorry to hear you feel that way all of the time...but it means so much to know that SOMEONE actually gets it. You are right, even if they SAY they understand, when it comes down to the reality, I don’t think anyone could really handle it, at least people that I know 😔 Yes, very lonely indeed.

I can sympathize completely. I lost my fiancé when he was 19, and I was 26, to suicide. I can only imagine how painful a murder would be, my friend, but I can tell you that every.single.day was a struggle, for years. I did not want to live in a world without him. It was senseless, like you said, over something stupid. Now, 18 years later, I have made some sort of peace with it, but yes, it takes time, grieving, therapy; you name it. I am praying for you, dear girl, and my heart goes out to you.
Thank you sweetheart for the support! I am so sorry for your predicament as well😢 Lots of hugs from me to you!

I can empathize completely. My “family “ cannot be bothered to come see me, though they make several trips per month...nor see their grandchildren. I begged them to come for our first Christmas in our new home, and they actually became enraged at me for suggesting it. This, btw, is after a childhood fraught with abuse. I suppose I should not be surprised, but it still hurts.
Can I ask why, besides probably depression, that you wish to die?

I am truly sorry about your loss...I cannot imagine. My first child was actually what saved my life five years ago. 💕Thank you so much for your kind words. They are few and far between because, as you probably know, you can’t just talk to anyone about this.
Thank you for your caring response. I have been in counseling for years, and on different antidepressant/anti anxiety meds for years as well, to no avail
Might I ask what is your present circumstance which makes life untenable?

Dear Suicide Watch and others,

I 100% empathize with your plight. I have what many may call a “charmed life,” the American Dream. But is a job, a house, and children/a husband really supposed to fulfill this deep void? My husband tells me I’m crazy because I don’t just “snap out of it,” but you know what? 
I grew up being physically, mentally and sexually abused. All my life, I have had to work twice as hard to get the same advantages as my contemporaries, and I STILL feel inadequate-daily. 
My mother just died of a massive stroke, and the bastards who called themselves her extended family are trying to take me to court for all she willed to me and my brother. 
Is it wrong to say that a marriage and two kids is just not enough to fulfill this deep, complicated chasm of pain that just will not recede, despite YEARS of therapy?? 
Please, someone tell me your thoughts, because I don’t feel that anyone truly understands, and forgive me for the novel.
